title.en: Boss case: After the kidney transplant

boss.case: A 45-year-old man received a deceased-donor kidney transplant 3 months ago. He takes tacrolimus, mycophenolate and prednisone. He now has new tremor and BP 160/95 mm Hg, and creatinine has risen from 1.2 to 1.8 mg/dL.

o: Binding FKBP → inhibiting calcineurin → ↓ IL-2 transcription

qs.q: His tremor, hypertension and rising creatinine suggest:
qs.e: Check trough level; biopsy may be needed to exclude rejection.

qs.q: A drug that would raise tacrolimus levels:
qs.e: Inducers lower levels and risk rejection.

o: Inhibiting IMP dehydrogenase → ↓ guanine synthesis in lymphocytes

qs.q: Which immunosuppressant is nephro-sparing and may replace tacrolimus?
qs.e: Sirolimus is not nephrotoxic but causes hyperlipidemia and poor wound healing.

steps.e: Lymphocytes rely on de novo guanine synthesis.

steps.e: Mycophenolate is teratogenic; azathioprine is acceptable.
